tigerman325
2020-03-22 17:46 GMT+1

A single doesn't have 5 different tracks unless they are remixes of the same basic track. Look at the Beatles, etc. There are tons of examples in which there was an EP version released in UK and a single version released at the same time that only had 2 tracks. A single can be more than 2 tracks if they all have the same basic recording, Your example of the remixes points this out. The EP you are merging to the single has 5 unique tracks. That is a textbook example of an EP. Now, I personally thank all remix singles should be different from basic singles, but that's a whole other discussion that is more controversial than this one.

https://musicbrainz.org/doc/Release_Group/Type
It's possible to make the argument that is's a maxi-single I suppose, but I never really thought those were prevalent until CD single releases.

https://musicbrainz.org/doc/Style/Release_Group
Other situations
There are a number of situations where there is currently no consensus about whether releases should be grouped together or not. This includes the same album sung in different languages, re-recorded albums and remixed albums. Be aware that attempting to group these releases can be quite controversial. If in doubt, these releases should probably be in separate release groups.

Discogs always groups EP & Singles together, MB doesn't.
